findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.
findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.

findings.evidence: Archiving "Design System Refresh" will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team. You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list.
findings.violation: The copy names the archived projects list as where the project can be restored, but the artifact defines no such state and no link or control anywhere targets one; the stated reversal path does not exist in the artifact as specified.
findings.fix: Either add an archived projects list state with a restore control that this link resolves to, or remove the restore claim from the archive-confirm copy if no reversal path is being specified.

findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.
findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.

findings.evidence: the "project-settings" section's form has one button, id "project-settings-save-btn", type "submit", text "Save"; the section defines no success message, no confirmation text, and no state transition following this button.
findings.violation: This action changes stored state, the project's name, but the artifact specifies no in-progress or result feedback beyond the field's own retained value: no confirmation message, no changed control state, and no defined next state after the button is activated.
findings.fix: Add a confirmation message or a visibly changed control state after "Save" is activated, for example "Saved" text near the button or a timestamp update.

findings.evidence: the "invite-member" section's form has a "Save" button, type "submit", with no defined action or next state; the section separately offers the "invite-member-continue-link" link, text "Continue", targeting "#invite-sent", outside the form.
findings.violation: The form's "Save" button, the control that would plausibly commit the entered email, defines no result: no confirmation, no next state, and no stated relation to the separate "Continue" link, which is the only control in the artifact whose target reaches the "invite-sent" confirmation state. A user has no way to tell from the artifact whether activating "Save" sends the invite, or whether "Continue" must also be activated.
findings.fix: State explicitly what "Save" does, for example remove it if "Continue" alone commits and sends the invite, and add a confirmation or changed control state after whichever control actually sends the invite.

findings.evidence: An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.
findings.violation: This state refers to "the address entered above" but the "invite-sent" section is its own defined state with no email address displayed anywhere in it; a user cannot verify which address received the invite without navigating back to the "invite-member" section.
findings.fix: Display the invited email address on the "invite-sent" state itself, for example "An invite was sent to name@example.com."

findings.evidence: The last import finished with 2 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 15 and 99 were skipped; every other row was imported.
findings.violation: This message names what went wrong, rows 15 and 99 referenced a nonexistent project, but the section's only control is "Back to your projects"; no control lets the user retry the import, review the source file, or resolve the two skipped rows from this state.
findings.fix: Add a control on the "import-status" state that lets the user retry the import or view and fix the two skipped rows, for example a "Retry import" or "View skipped rows" control.
